---
title: "Gradient Clipping"
description: "A technique that limits gradient magnitude before applying a parameter update."
term: "Gradient Clipping"
letter: "G"
category: "Model Training"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Gradient clipping limits unusually large gradients during training. It
can prevent a single update from changing model parameters too
dramatically.

## Technical explanation

With global norm clipping and threshold $c$, a gradient vector $g$ can
be rescaled as
$g' = g\min(1,c/\|g\|)$. Value clipping instead clamps each gradient
component independently. These methods change the update and should be
selected with awareness of the optimizer and training dynamics.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Clipping can stabilize training when gradients occasionally become
large, especially in recurrent or deep networks. It is a mitigation
technique, not a substitute for diagnosing poor scaling, numerical
errors, or an unsuitable learning rate.

## How it works

After gradients are computed and before the optimizer update, the
training loop measures their norm or values and applies the configured
limit. The optimizer then uses the modified gradients to update
parameters.

## Practical example

If a training run has sporadic large gradient norms, global norm
clipping can cap those updates while retaining the direction of the
gradient vector.

## Common misconceptions

- Gradient clipping does not guarantee convergence.
- Norm clipping and value clipping are different operations.
- A clipping threshold that is too low can suppress useful learning
  signals.
